newsitem.title: UK: Monthly Review - Algerian slaughter, East Europe erupts.
newsitem.headline: Monthly Review - Algerian slaughter, East Europe erupts.

text.p: Street protests swelled across the Balkans as opposition movements gathered strength and kept up the momentum of daily massed rallies in town centres.

In Bulgaria crowds demanded new elections, opposition protesters kept up pressure on Serbia's Socialist government over annulled election results and Albanians demonstrated over their government's handling of failed pyramid savings schemes.

Moslem fundamentalists in Algeria stepped up attacks during the month of Ramadam, killing about 180 people. The country's top union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda, a retired general and a 13-month old baby were among the latest to be killed.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
Jan 1 - An Israeli soldier opens fire in a crowded Hebron market, wounding seven Palestinians.
Jan 2 - The tanker Nakhodka carrying 19,000 tonnes (133,000 barrels) of fuel oil breaks in stormy seas off the coast of Japan.
Jan 2 - Libya executes six senior officers and two civilians for spying, saying they used equipment supplied by the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA).
Jan 3 - Jewish settlers agree to leave a West Bank hilltop they had occupied, ending a tense standoff with Israeli police.
Jan 3 - President Bill Clinton again delays implementation of the so-called Helms-Burton law that would allow U.S. citizens to sue some foreign companies doing business in Communist-ruled Cuba.
Jan 5 - Russia withdraws the last of its defence ministry troops from Chechnya, marking a formal end to Moscow's ill-fated military campaign in the region.
Jan 7 - Former East German spymaster Markus Wolf goes on trial charged with kidnapping.
Jan 8 - British tycoon Richard Branson fails in his attempt to be the first balloonist to fly round the world, a day after takeoff. Swiss-Belgian attempt takes off on January 12 and fails same day.
Jan 9 - Afghan opposition forces of General Abdul Rashid Dostum launch a big offensive against the Islamic Taleban militia in northwestern Afghanistan.
Jan 9 - In Sri Lanka, Tamil Tigers attack the town of Paranthan; Defence Ministry says Tigers were repulsed suffering 350 killed with 223 government soldiers killed.
Jan 9 - Two bombs apparently planted by Arab guerrillas explode near Tel Aviv's central bus station, wounding at least 13 people.
Jan 10 - Anti-government protesters break into the building housing Bulgaria's parliament during a protest to demand early parliamentary elections.
Jan 11 - Serbian government gives in to demands that opposition victories in disputed elections be restored, agreeing with protesting students that the results must be honoured.
Jan 12 - Sudanese rebels begin attacks along the eastern borders of the country.
Jan 14 - Election commissions reinstate opposition victories in Belgrade city assembly and Nis, Serbia's second largest city.
Jan 15 - Israel and the PLO conclude a long-elusive agreement extending Palestinian rule to Hebron.
Jan 16 - The Islamic Taleban captures the strategic Bagram military airbase north of Kabul.
Jan 17 - Israeli soldiers hand the headquarters of their 30-year-long occupation to Palestinian police.
Jan 18 - South Korean strike leaders abandon calls for indefinite stoppages in protest at a controversial labour law.
Jan 18 - A bomb explodes outside a courthouse in the Pakistani city of Lahore, killing 26 people including the leader of the SSP militant Sunni Moslem group.
Jan 18 - Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky resigns after nearly 11 years in power.

Jan 18 - 36 people are massacred in a series of killings in remote villages in Algeria. The next day 23 people die when a bomb explodes in the centre of Algiers. On the 21st, six people die when a car bomb explodes in the centre of Algiers.
Jan 19 - Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrives in Hebron to lay claim to most of the city.
Jan 20 - U.S. adventurer Steve Fossett falls short of his dream to become the first person to fly non-stop around the world in a balloon.
Jan 20 - President Yeltsin leaves hospital after having treatment for pneumonia.
Jan 20 - President Bill Clinton is formally sworn in for a second four-year term.
Jan 21 - South Korean President Kim Young-sam agrees to send a controversial labour law back to parliament.
Jan 21 - German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus sign a joint declaration meant to cement post-war reconciliation between the two neighbours.
Jan 21 - U.S. House of Representatives votes to reprimand Speaker Newt Gingrich and order him to pay $300,000 for violating House rules.
Jan 22 - The space shuttle Atlantis lands, ending a four-month orbital odyssey for astronaut John Blaha aboard the Russian space station Mir.
Jan 24 - German tennis star Steffi Graf's father is sentenced to three years and nine months in jail for tax evasion.
Jan 25 - A fire in a karaoke club in Hong Kong kills 17 people.
Jan 25 - Central African Republic president Ange-Felix Patasse signs a peace deal with rivals to end an army mutiny and ethnic bloodshed.
Jan 26 - Albanians who lost their life savings in a pyramid investment scheme set buildings ablaze and fight riot police.
Jan 27 - Switzerland's ambassador to the U.S. resigns after a document he wrote calling for "waging war" against Jewish groups was leaked.
Jan 27 - Serbia's opposition loses a court battle over control of Belgrade after disputed local elections but takes power in Nis.
Jan 27 - President Boris Yeltsin cancels plans to visit the Netherlands on doctors' orders, deepening concern about his health.
Jan 28 - South African police officers confess to the murder of Steve Biko in 1977, and ask the Truth and Reconciliation Commission for an amnesty.
Jan 28 - Guerrilla chief Aslan Maskhadov claims victory in Chechnya's presidential election.
Jan 29 - Pakistan's Supreme Court upholds last November's dismissal of prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
Jan 31 - South Korean state prosecutors arrest Chung Tae-soo, founder of the stricken Hanbo group.

Notable Deaths; Prince Bertil of Sweden (5th); Sandor Vegh, violinist and conductor (8); Alvino Misciano, Italian tenor (10); James Dickey, U.S. writer (19); Colonel Parker, manager of Elvis Presley (21); Abdelhak Benhamouda, Algerian trade union leader (28).
